newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq drops in sympathy with Dow.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq drops in sympathy with Dow.

text.p: Nasdaq shares dropped Monday, after a decline in the Dow industrials and bonds, traders said.

The Nasdaq composite index lost 12.77 points or 0.88 percent to close unofficially at 1434.33. Nasdaq shares traded as high as 1451.07, approaching a new record high, but later lost steam as the Dow industrials dropped 192 points to 7604.
"It's mostly in sympathy with the Dow. Once the Dow kept sliding, the Nasdaq couldn't hold on to its gains," said Patrick Davis, head of over-the-counter trading at Salomon Brothers.
The Dow industrials dropped in a wave profit-taking sparked by comments from the Japanese Prime Minister about the potential sale of U.S. government securities by Japan, traders said.
"Pretty much everything was down. The big tech names, which trade almost like blue chips, had a hard holding on to last week's gains when there's so much pressure on today," another trader said.
Declining issues beat gainers, 2402 to 1977, on total volume of nearly 563 million shares. Nasdaq shares have showed gains in seven of the previous 10 sessions.
